obligations.subject: Watching
obligations.question: Audit peer observation lane and forwarding in both wrapper orders.
obligations.decision: Retain Watching as-is; evidence verified. Classification: the peer-observation event sum WatchEvent (Inner(E) | PeerStopped) is a typed-sum derivation over the neutral protocol vocabulary (PeerEvent trait), the ObservePeer service request is a Bombay-derived ServiceSends lane appended as the own half of a SendProduct, and the reaction selection (peer-equality guard, stop_on_abnormal_death outcome classes) is deliberate Bombay policy. Forwarding in both wrapper orders is lawful: WatchEvent delegates TimeEvent/ChildEvent/WorkerEvent/ShutdownEvent/UserEvent to Inner, and the dual AtEvent delegates PeerEvent to Inner, so no order drops or relabels a lane.

obligations.subject: Supervising and Proxy
obligations.question: Audit failure reactions, worker/proxy routing, replacement provenance, and nesting.
obligations.decision: Retain Supervising and Proxy as-is; evidence verified. Classification: supervision is a Bombay-derived construction over the pure fold (per module doc supervising.rs:1-10, one typed WorkerStopped observation updates explicit slot state and returns only sends/creates/become); stable child identity via a proxy actor with generation-scoped worker nonces is the Bombay derivation of Erlang-style supervision; Strategy/RestartPolicy eligibility, candidate sets, budget admission (RestartDenial::BudgetExceeded) and the default retire_on_supervision_failure reaction are deliberate Bombay policy. Replacement provenance is carried by CreationKind::ReplacementIncarnation emitted only by Proxy, and WorkerEvent/ReportWorkerStopped routing keeps proxy identity stable across worker restarts.

obligations.subject: mixed wrapper orders
obligations.question: Prove supported nesting drops, duplicates, reorders, relabels, or reinterprets no lane.
obligations.decision: Retain the supported mixed nesting as-is; evidence verified. Classification: lane preservation is a typed-sum/typed-product derivation — every wrapper event sum is Inner(E) plus its own variants, every foreign-lane trait impl forwards via E::lane(event).map(Self::Inner) without reconstructing the payload (no relabel/reinterpretation), and every wrapper's send algebra merges inner actions as SendProduct{inner, own} (no drop/duplicate); initialization accumulation is innermost-first by construction (each layer wraps the already-wrapped inner actions and appends only its own lane, Supervising then extends with the configured fleet).
